sections.translation: A **multimedia web server** is a third-party service that receives the audio broadcast from the **MX2200** and retransmits it via a public link accessible anywhere in the world, simultaneously to multiple devices. - Subscription is typically based on the **number of simultaneous users** supported. - Once access is configured on the console, usage is very simple: the MX2200 just needs to be connected to the Internet and the broadcast started. - It is an ideal method when **mass distribution of the signal** is required. The **latency** in this type of transmission can vary between **5 and 30 seconds**, depending on the platform and connection. For this reason, it is only recommended when the signal is generated from the remote location **without real-time interaction** with the studios. --- Turn the **encoder** to the **CONNECTION CENTER** screen and press it to enter. Navigate with the encoder, select **HTTP STREAM** and press to open the option. On the control screen, select **YES** to initiate the link with the web server.\ When the connection is established, the **CONNECTION CENTER** and **HOME** screens will show **HTTP STREAM ENABLED**. Repeat the procedure and select **NO** to disable the transmission. Receiving a transmission via web server is the simplest method: - The service provider provides an **http link**. - The link can be opened from **any web browser** on a PC, tablet, or smartphone. - No additional configurations are required at the studios. This method is ideal for **public streaming** of a station or event, allowing global access without the need for specialized software on the listeners' part.
